citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: company description
citations.excerpt: Gambit Security keeps enterprises operating through disruption.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: summary
citations.excerpt: A financially motivated operator is running three open source AI harnesses against hundreds of online retailers, almost entirely unattended.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: September window
citations.excerpt: Between 10 and 15 September alone, 105 attack projects were launched and at least 27 companies were compromised to varying degrees.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: the three harnesses
citations.excerpt: The operator used three AI harnesses: Strix for vulnerability search, Cairn for autonomous end-to-end exploitation, and Hermes to orchestrate the campaign, launch intrusion jobs, steer the activity and give tactical guidance in the impact and other stages.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: Hermes state
citations.excerpt: Hermes is an open source autonomous AI agent with a persistent memory, skills that the agent writes and edits itself, a searchable archive of past sessions, scheduled jobs and a web console.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: human prompts
citations.excerpt: The human prompts are short instructions in Chinese, usually launching an attack, tasking the agent with a general next step, or what to do next after achieving access.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: Cairn engine
citations.excerpt: Cairn is an autonomous penetration testing engine. It receives target domains and an objective, such as to get a shell or admin access, then runs for hours until it achieves the objective, times out, or is stopped.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: handed credentials
citations.excerpt: Others were picked by hand or by other means, such as a New Zealand retailer and a US photo printing company that they handed to the agent already holding a working administrator password

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: AI claims caveat
citations.excerpt: While AI claims and reporting may turn out to be inaccurate, we rely on them in this report because we could verify substantial parts of the claims by the first two methods, which showed them to be accurate.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: interim report
citations.excerpt: The following is an interim report of our findings.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: possible errors
citations.excerpt: Nevertheless, due to the scale, incomplete data and early stage of the analysis, a few errors or inaccuracies are possible.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: deleted projects
citations.excerpt: The chart below shows the state of 48 of them. The other 57 were deleted and not available for analysis.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: per-company cost
citations.excerpt: Spread over the companies attacked, this is a marginal cost of a few US dollars to a few tens of US dollars for each targeted company.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: TL;DR
citations.excerpt: An investigation by NorForge into publicly exposed AI-driven penetration-testing control panels has uncovered how they are extensively used in malicious cyber operations.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: vantage
citations.excerpt: We bring our extensive sandboxing expertise to AI agents, so you can see everything your agents do

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: malicious panels
citations.excerpt: More than 20 exposed Cairn panels were identified as likely associated with malicious activity, providing an unusually detailed view of how threat actors select targets, direct autonomous agents, exploit vulnerabilities, and establish persistent access to compromised systems.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: red team exposure
citations.excerpt: In addition, a considerable number of apparently legitimate red team operations were also exposed this way, potentially placing clients at risk.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: scan method
citations.excerpt: Quick searches using the Shodan and Censys search engines reveal hosts running what appear to be AI harnesses of different kinds. Most need authorization to access. Most. But there are quite a few of these interfaces left open by their operators.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: what panels reveal
citations.excerpt: However; it is the nature of these panels that they reveal a great deal of sensitive information about the targets; including who they are, what weaknesses have been uncovered, account secrets and API keys, and whether they have been compromised or not.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: blackboard
citations.excerpt: The agent posts every fact onto a project-internal blackboard. A human operator can also add their own hints to the same blackboard.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: panel contents
citations.excerpt: They detail everything that the agent has discovered in the process, and if that was not enough, they include human input that includes credentials harvested elsewhere.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: secrets scan
citations.excerpt: We ran the secrets scanner Trufflehog over the data from these Cairn instances.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: secrets found
citations.excerpt: Literally hundreds of secrets of different kinds, from relatively trivial to extremely serious; with 11% verified valid by Trufflehog.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: unprotected controls
citations.excerpt: These panels appear completely unprotected, exposing what looks like the full administrative functionality of the harness.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: exposure regardless of outcome
citations.excerpt: In other words, having your site tested on an open Cairn instance is often a serious security issue, regardless of outcome of the test.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: red team nightmare
citations.excerpt: This has also proven to be a problem for legitimate red teams; gathering secrets from your client just to publish them on the Internet is a nightmare scenario.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: claim verified
citations.excerpt: Just to test, we checked if one of the claimed intrusions had really happened by fetching the shell URL mentioned in a completed task against a large hardware parts vendor. The URL did indeed serve an uploader webshell.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: success rate
citations.excerpt: But it is a reasonable assumption that for the harnesses we have seen in these campaigns, average success rate is hovering around 10%, with many of the remaining tasks achieving partial goals, or are able to gather information that can be used in later attempts.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: time to goal
citations.excerpt: If we concentrate on the tasks that did reach their goals, especially on the AIA0001 cluster which most resembles general purpose intrusion activity, we can now see that the average time from project start to goal met was a little under 23 hours, generating on average 140 facts per project.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: snapshot caveat
citations.excerpt: It is also worth noting that this is a snapshot at this point in time. Models and harnesses evolve very quickly.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: cost estimate
citations.excerpt: We estimate the average cost of a task to end up around $5 if one includes unsuccessful, early ending projects.

citations.label: NorForge, Inside Cairn exposed AI pentesting panels: cost uncertainty
citations.excerpt: The uncertainty here is however considerable, and numbers could be off by a clear margin.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: staging server evidence
citations.excerpt: First, direct evidence we found on the attacker’s staging server, such as the exfiltrated data itself and respective tooling.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: logs and AI claims
citations.excerpt: Third, logs and AI claims found on the attacker’s server.

citations.label: Gambit Security, AI agents hacking online retailers: documented Cairn chain
citations.excerpt: the chain below was documented in one completed Cairn project: Unauthenticated SQLi (login email param, error-based EXTRACTVALUE) -> OTP plaintext read from the OTP table (MFA bypass) -> admin panel access -> Arbitrary file upload (image field, no extension check) -> host RCE (uid=1001, gid=root) -> sudo NOPASSWD python3.12 -> root -> NFS mount (internal address, no_root_squash) -> WP blog DB credentials from wp-config.php on NFS -> WP admin write (new user via DB) -> WP plugin upload -> blog host RCE -> AWS Secrets Manager full dump (46 secrets, 102KB)
